name: Work and Employment Permit (Employer-Sponsored)

requirements.blocker_text: Law on Granting Permit for Work and Employment of Foreign Citizens: the employer submits the application (Article 16), which must include certification from the Employment Office that no jobseeker registered in Kosovo meets the position's requirements (Article 16.1.5, the labor-market test). Separately, the Government sets an annual quota of employment permits for foreign nationals by 15 December of the preceding year (Article 4) -- meaning the permit is unavailable outside the quota regardless of individual merit. A decision issues within 30 days of a complete submission (Article 20); the employer must then sign the employment contract within 15 days of the permit being issued (Article 18). Permit type B (the standard employment permit) is issued yearly and is renewable; Type A (minimum 6 months) and Type C (5 years, for those who already held a Type B) also exist. A refused applicant may appeal within 8 days (Article 21).
requirements.fix_path: Have the employer obtain the Employment Office's no-local-candidate certification and file within the annual government quota; sign the employment contract within 15 days of permit issuance.

evidence_required.document: Employer's written request with supporting documents
Employment Office certification (no qualified local jobseeker available)
Signed employment contract (within 15 days of permit issuance)

outcome.duration_length: 6 months (Type A) to 1 year renewable (Type B) to 5 years for prior Type B holders (Type C)

sources.title: Republic of Kosovo (official government-hosted primary legal text) -- Law on Granting Permit for Work and Employment of Foreign Citizens, Articles 4, 7, 16, 18, 20-21

notes: NEW COUNTRY BUILD (Kosovo). STATUS: PUBLISHED -- hard requirement sourced directly to Kosovo's own government-hosted primary legal text, tier 1. GENUINE FINDING: Kosovo runs BOTH a labor-market test AND a hard annual government quota set by mid-December for the following year -- meaning even a fully-qualified applicant can be blocked simply because the year's quota is exhausted, a double gate not seen in most other countries built in this dataset. leads_to_pr set to true and pr_after_months to 60, reflecting the general permanent-residence threshold confirmed by Kosovo Police's border brochure (5 years of uninterrupted temporary residence, reduced to 3 if married to a Kosovo citizen or permanent resident -- see xk_family_reunification.json) -- Kosovo is one of the few countries in this recent run of builds (after Bosnia, Mali, Niger, Haiti) with an actual, confirmed temporary-to-permanent residence ladder rather than a single undifferentiated status. dual_citizenship_allowed set to true per Article 3 of Kosovo's (2008-vintage) citizenship law -- see xk_citizenship_naturalisation.json for the fuller picture and the disclosed uncertainty about whether this specific provision survived the law's two subsequent replacements. family_can_work left null: not addressed by the source.
